**Body (as-new):**

```markdown
## Context

A customer support review triggered this ask. Today a report can be downloaded or emailed.

## Problem

The first download from an emailed report is empty, so the recipient wastes a retry before getting the data. A 12-row report downloads as zero rows the first time and as 12 rows when retried later.

Downloads leave out the report's final row, so recipients work from incomplete totals. A four-row report shows four rows on screen but downloads as three.

One delivery request sends the email twice, so recipients have to check whether the two reports differ. One request produces two emails that carry the same file.

The email subject names the previous day's report, so recipients misfile today's work. A report requested on October 21 arrives with a subject naming October 20, although the attached file is October 21's.

## Idea

The reporter proposes fixing report delivery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given a 12-row report delivered by email, when the recipient downloads it for the first time, the download contains 12 rows.
- [ ] Given a four-row report that shows four rows on screen, when it is downloaded, the download contains all four rows.
- [ ] Given one delivery request for an emailed report, when the request is processed, exactly one email is sent.
- [ ] Given a report requested on October 21, when it is emailed, the email subject names October 21.
```

## Proposed body — as new

### Context

A customer support review triggered this request. Today, reports can be downloaded or emailed.

### Problem

The first emailed download is empty, forcing recipients to retry. For example, a 12-row report initially downloads as zero rows, then downloads as 12 rows on a later retry.

Downloads omit the final row, leaving recipients with incomplete totals. For example, a four-row report downloads as three rows even though the fourth row appears on screen.

One delivery request sends duplicate emails, making recipients check whether the reports differ. For example, one request sends two emails containing the same file.

The email subject names yesterday’s report, causing recipients to misfile today’s work. For example, an October 21 request produces an October 20 subject even though the attached file is for October 21.

### Idea

The reporter proposes fixing report delivery.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given a 12-row report, when a recipient requests email delivery and downloads the report from the first email, the first download contains the report’s 12 rows without requiring a retry.
- [ ] Given a report with four rows visible on screen, when a recipient downloads it, the download contains those four rows, including the final row.
- [ ] Given a report, when a recipient makes one email delivery request, exactly one report email is sent.
- [ ] Given a report for October 21, when email delivery is requested on October 21, the email subject names October 21 rather than October 20.

---
